intentions.title: One binary serves both the `bp` CLI and the interactive Miller-columns TUI, routed by argv shape
intentions.evidence: main.go: `len(os.Args) > 1` dispatches to cli.Execute (CLI face); no args launches runTUI() (Sanity-Desk-style TUI). Shared apiclient/DataStore underneath both faces; cli.ExitOpenDesk sentinel lets a login-connect CLI flow hand off straight into the TUI desk.

intentions.title: Give the terminal a Sanity Studio Structure Builder-equivalent so the desk tree is declared with the same chainable vocabulary (List/ListItem/DocumentTypeList/Document/Divider)
intentions.evidence: structure.go header explicitly maps S.list()/S.listItem()/S.documentTypeList()/S.documentTypeListItem()/S.document()/S.divider() to Go builders producing a StructureNode tree that panes resolve against.

intentions.title: Follow the exact same active-server resolution and perspective as the `bp` CLI so `bp use prod` moves the TUI too
intentions.evidence: main.go runTUI: cfg := cli.ResolvedAPIConfig() — flags > BARKPARK_* env > saved-config active server > baked defaults; reads BARKPARK_PERSPECTIVE (drafts default); first-run/no-server states are intercepted before any network call (cli.FirstRun(), cli.LoggedInWithoutServer()).

intentions.title: Give every draft a pre-publish confidence check: a live draft↔published field diff before shipping or discarding
intentions.evidence: diff.go: `d` on a focused draft editor fetches the published twin (GET /v1/data/doc/…) and diffs against dirty-aware editor state; +/- rows reuse ok/danger status hues by convention (comment forbids minting new diff tokens prematurely); inert with a status message when there's nothing to compare.

intentions.title: Surface full document revision history in the terminal, read-only by design — restore stays in Studio/API
intentions.evidence: history.go: `H` opens GET /v1/data/history/<ds>/<type>/<bare-id>; enter on a row opens the diff modal over the list (revision vs current); explicit design note: 'a destructive overwrite earns more ceremony than a terminal modal in v1' — no restore action here.

intentions.title: Bring Studio's bulk publish/unpublish workflow (multi-select + batch mutate) to the doc-list pane
intentions.evidence: bulk.go: space marks/unmarks a doc-list row keyed by bare published id (survives draft↔published id flips); ctrl+p/U act on the whole marked set; partial-success semantics (failures counted, first error shown) mirror Studio's E3 bulk-publish behavior.

intentions.title: Render Papers/PortableDoc content inside the TUI through the same pdrender registry and theme used elsewhere, read-only, at a comfortable centered measure
intentions.evidence: paper.go: paperColumnWidth caps to maxPaperWidth=100 and centers; barkparkPaperTheme() derives from styles.go palette vars (highlight, dimText, editorLabelStyle) rather than pdrender's private theme copies, so TUI restyling propagates automatically; comment states 'a paper is READ-ONLY in the TUI — edits happen in Studio'.

intentions.title: Let users pick reference-field targets via a searchable modal that writes the exact wire format Studio's own reference selector writes
intentions.evidence: refpicker.go: enter on a reference field opens a picker over documents of the field's RefType; stores the bare published id (drafts. stripped) matching Content.published_id; live case-insensitive filter typing; refTitles cache renders id + resolved title.

intentions.title: Give the desk a full-text search overlay hitting the same scoped search endpoint Studio and the API expose, without mutating pane/focus state
intentions.evidence: search.go: `/` opens a query prompt, hits GET /w/<ws>/p/<proj>/v1/data/search/<dataset>; results render as a transient modal that drills into a hit's editor by _type; zero hits never open an empty modal.

intentions.title: Gracefully degrade the multi-pane Miller-columns layout to single-column on narrow terminals instead of breaking
intentions.evidence: tui.go constants: minEditorWidth(40)/minEditorUsable(24)/minFrameWidth(16)/minTitleWithBadge(10) drive tiered degradation — drop list columns before shrinking the editor below usable width, drop badges before truncating titles, and fall back to a one-line 'too small' message below minFrameWidth.
